Static diagnosis points to `org.joda.time.chrono.GJChronology` as the source of all five failures.

The primary bug is in `GJChronology.convertByYear(long, Chronology, Chronology)` at [GJChronology.java](/abs/path/GJChronology.java:83). It copies `from.year().get(instant)` directly into `to.getDateTimeMillis(...)`:

```java
return to.getDateTimeMillis(
    from.year().get(instant),
    from.monthOfYear().get(instant),
    from.dayOfMonth().get(instant),
    from.millisOfDay().get(instant));
```

That is wrong when converting Gregorian results across the BCE boundary into Julian chronology, because Julian has no year `0`. The stack trace confirms this path:
`LocalDate.plusYears` -> `GJChronology$ImpreciseCutoverField.add` -> `GJChronology.gregorianToJulianByYear` -> `GJChronology.convertByYear` -> `JulianChronology.adjustYearForSet`.
This explains:
